Incremental Cash Flow Return over Equity over 3 Years

Volatility of accruals; higher values suggest higher risk of earnings manipulation or lower earnings quality
Rate at which intangible assets are amortized; higher rates may indicate more aggressive accounting practices
Change in the number of analysts covering the stock; higher values indicate increased attention from analysts
Change in asset turnover ratio, reflecting changes in efficiency in using assets to generate sales
Ratio of capital expenditures to depreciation; higher values suggest greater reinvestment in assets relative to depreciation
Ratio of capital expenditures to sales; higher values indicate larger capital spending as a proportion of revenues
Ratio of operating cash flow to total debt, measuring how well cash flow covers debt obligations; higher is safer
Ratio of convertible debt to total debt; higher values mean more debt that may dilute shareholders if converted

Period-over-period change in deferred revenue (often advance payments for goods/services not yet delivered); higher value may indicate aggressive revenue recognition practices or increased prepayments
Change in Deferred Tax Assets [ Descending] - [Quality.Aggressive Accounting]
Change in Deferred Tax Liabilities [ Descending] - [Quality.Aggressive Accounting]
Change in Depreciation Rate [ Ascending] - [Quality.Aggressive Accounting]

A measure of how consistent, stable, or “smooth” reported earnings are; higher smoothness can indicate either reliable profitability or, less desirably, earnings management (manipulation of results for perceived stability)
The effective average interest rate that the company pays on its outstanding debt; a higher rate signals increased financial leverage or perceived credit risk

Volatility (variability) of analyst EPS forecast errors, measuring how often and how much analysts’ EPS predictions deviate from actual results; higher values indicate lower forecasting quality and possibly greater earnings uncertainty
Volatility (variability) of reported earnings per share over time; higher values imply less stable profitability and greater financial risk
Degree to which shareholders’ interests are diluted, typically via new equity issuance or convertible securities; higher value shows greater capital raising at potential shareholder expense
Ratio of finished goods inventory to total inventory, with higher values suggesting slower inventory turnover, possible demand weakness, or inefficient working capital management
Period-over-period change in gross margin (gross profit as a % of sales); an increase signals improved efficiency or profitability, while a decrease indicates margin compression
Volatility of gross margin over time, measuring stability in core profitability; higher values mean less predictable gross profitability, which signals operational risk
Ratio of income statement (accrual) tax to cash taxes paid; larger discrepancies may suggest earnings management, aggressive accounting, or timing differences between book and cash tax reporting
Amount of interest and investment income earned by the company, reflecting non-operating income; higher values may indicate lower earnings quality or greater reliance on non-core activities
Change in inventory levels over the relevant period, indicating how much inventory increased or decreased; large changes may reflect working capital management quality
Number of days inventory is held before being sold or used; higher values suggest slower inventory turnover and potential working capital risk
Change in labor efficiency, measuring improvement or deterioration in company productivity from its workforce; higher values indicate increased efficiency
Minority Interest to Equity [ Descending] - [Quality.Earnings quality]
Net operating assets, representing the company’s operating assets minus operating liabilities, reflecting capital utilization efficiency
Amount of non-operating income (not from core business) relative to EBITDA; higher values may indicate lower earnings quality or unsustainable income sources
Number of days the company takes to pay its suppliers (accounts payable days); higher values mean longer payment cycles and indicate working capital management strategy and risk
Amount of pension obligation (projected benefit obligation) expressed as a debt equivalent; higher values signal greater pension-related liability risk
Discount rate used to value pension liabilities; higher rates lower reported liabilities but may indicate aggressive accounting practices
Value of pension and other benefit obligations relative to total enterprise value (TEV); higher values imply greater risk from pension liabilities when compared to company size
Ratio of pension expense to EBITDA, indicating the magnitude of pension costs relative to operational profitability; higher values suggest higher pension-related risk or liability
Total annual pension interest cost, reflecting the cost of maintaining pension obligations; higher levels may signal aggressive accounting or greater pension financial burden
Ratio of projected benefit obligation (total pension liability estimate) to total enterprise value (TEV); measures the scale of pension liabilities relative to firm enterprise value
Ratio of prepaid expenses to sales, quantifying advance payments (for goods/services not yet received) as a fraction of revenue; potentially highlights aggressive accounting
Period-over-period change in accounts receivable, indicating shifts in revenue collection or potential earnings manipulation through receivables
Average number of days it takes a company to collect its accounts receivable; higher values indicate slower collections and possible working capital risks
Ratio of recurring (serial) special items or charges to sales; higher values signal repeated unusual or non-operating expenses, suggesting lower earnings quality
Ratio of selling, general & administrative expenses (SG&A) to sales or revenues; measures overhead efficiency, with higher values implying less operational efficiency
Volatility (variability) of SG&A expenses over time, with higher readings indicating unstable or unpredictable overhead costs
Ratio of short-term debt to total capitalization, assets, or related base; measures reliance on short-term financing and assesses leverage/liquidity risk
Effective tax rate (typically taxes paid as a percentage of pre-tax income); lower rates may suggest aggressive accounting or tax avoidance practices
Change in total debt outstanding (period-over-period), capturing increases or decreases in overall indebtedness and indicating changes in leverage or refinancing risk
Standardized measure of cash flow variability, with higher values indicating more unpredictable or volatile cash flows (higher risk)
Campbell, Hilscher, and Szilagyi's bankruptcy/default probability score, expressing the risk that the company will default, typically reported as a standardized z-score (higher = higher risk)
Montier’s C-Score, an integer-based forensic flag for possible earnings manipulation or accounting fraud, where higher values represent greater manipulation risk
Standardized measure of earnings variability, with higher values indicating more volatile or unpredictable earnings (higher risk)
Gross profit to total assets ratio, a profitability metric where higher values signify more efficient use of assets to generate gross profit
Incremental cash flow return on equity over the last 1 year, showing the change in cash flow returns to equity holders over a one-year period; higher is better
Incremental cash flow return on equity over the last 3 years, showing the change in cash flow returns to equity holders over three years; higher is better
Incremental cash flow return on equity over the last 5 years, reflecting long-term improvement or deterioration in cash flow returns to equity holders; higher is better
Mohanram G-score, an integer score (typically 0–6) quantifying fraud and earnings manipulation risk in growth stocks, with higher values signaling greater risk
Frequency count or flag indicating how often a company reports negative earnings over a defined historical period; higher values denote weaker profitability
Ohlson O-score, an accounting-based bankruptcy prediction score, where higher values signal higher bankruptcy risk based on financial statement inputs
Piotroski F-score (range 0–9), measuring fundamental/accounting quality, with higher values indicating better quality and financial strength
Wolfe Research’s proprietary composite score summarizing company quality and fraud/forensic risk, with higher values denoting better quality or lower risk
Ratio of illiquid or hard-to-sell assets to total assets, where higher levels imply more difficulty in asset liquidation, lower financial flexibility, or greater risk
Ratio of preferred equity to total capitalization or another base; gauges reliance on preferred stock in capital structure
